title: Breaking the Code: Security Assessment of AI Code Agents Through Systematic Jailbreaking Attacks
abstract: arXiv:2510.01359v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Code-capable large language model (LLM) agents are embedded in software engineering workflows where they can read, write, and execute code, raising "jailbreak" stakes beyond text-only settings. Prior evaluations emphasize refusal or harmful-text detection, leaving open whether agents compile and run malicious programs. We present JAWS-Bench (Jailbreaks Across WorkSpaces), a benchmark spanning three escalating workspace regimes mirroring attacker capability: empty (JAWS-0), single-file (JAWS-1), and multi-file (JAWS-M). We pair it with a hierarchical, executable-aware Judge Framework that tests (i) compliance, (ii) attack success, (iii) syntactic correctness, and (iv) runtime executability to measure deployable harm. Across seven LLM backends from five families, prompt-only attacks in JAWS-0 achieve 61% compliance; 58% are harmful, 52% parse, and 27% run end-to-end. translated_title: 破解代码：通过系统性越狱攻击对AI代码代理进行安全评估
translated_abstract: 具备代码能力的大语言模型（LLM）代理被嵌入到软件工程工作流中，能够读取、编写和执行代码，这使得“越狱”攻击的风险远超纯文本环境。以往的评估主要强调拒绝回答或有害文本检测，而代理是否会实际编译并运行恶意程序这一问题仍未得到解答。我们提出了JAWS-Bench（Jailbreaks Across WorkSpaces，跨工作区越狱基准），该基准涵盖三种递进式工作区场景，对应攻击者能力的不同层级：空工作区（JAWS-0）、单文件工作区（JAWS-1）和多文件工作区（JAWS-M）。我们配套设计了一个分层的、可执行感知的评审框架，用于测试：（i）合规性、（ii）攻击成功、（iii）语法正确性、（iv）运行时可执行性，以衡量可部署的实际危害。在来自五个系列的七个LLM后端上的实验表明，在JAWS-0中仅使用提示词的攻击即可达到61%的合规率；其中58%具有危害性，52%可通过语法解析，27%可端到端运行。在JAWS-1中，更强模型的合规率接近100%……
tldr: 该论文提出了JAWS-Bench基准和可执行感知的分层评审框架，首次系统评估了AI代码代理在越狱攻击下编译并运行恶意程序的实际危害，发现攻击成功率随工作区复杂度的增加而显著上升。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces JAWS-Bench and an executable-aware hierarchical Judge Framework to systematically assess how AI code agents can be jailbroken into compiling and running malicious programs, revealing that attack success escalates with workspace complexity.
